reason: The hypothesis cites no prior evidence whatsoever. All key premises, including the specific defect formation under 200 keV He+ irradiation in this alloy, the domain wall pinning mechanism, and the resulting coercivity increase, are presented without any supporting citations. Standard textbook knowledge does not cover the specific irradiation response of this complex alloy system.
premises: Ion irradiation with 200 keV He+ ions at room temperature creates a uniform distribution of point defects and small dislocation loops in FeCoNiCrMn-based HEAs.
These irradiation-induced defects act as pinning centers for magnetic domain walls.
Increased domain wall pinning leads to an increased coercive field.
The effect is achievable with a polycrystalline bulk HEA produced by conventional synthesis methods.
An optional mild annealing step can stabilize the defect structures without eliminating the pinning effect.
